title: Disabled math still rewrites LaTeX delimiters
reasoning: resolveLlmOutputContract computes mathEnabled from options.enableMath, but normalizeLatexMathDelimiters runs unconditionally. That means callers that pass enableMath: false still get \(...\) rewritten to $...$ and \[...\] rewritten to $$...$$ before rendering. The renderer later honors enableMath by choosing the non-math Marked instance, so disabled math can surface as altered literal text rather than preserving the provider output.
recommendation: Only call normalizeLatexMathDelimiters when mathEnabled is true, or remove enableMath from this contract if normalization is intentionally independent of math rendering.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for this feature, and the provided excerpts do not show coverage for enableMath=false behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a renderer infrastructure test that calls resolveLlmOutputContract('Use \\(x+1\\)', { enableMath: false }) and asserts the markdown remains unchanged, then verifies enableMath=true still normalizes delimiters.
minimumFixScope: Change resolveLlmOutputContract to gate delimiter normalization on mathEnabled and add focused tests for both enabled and disabled math paths.
